Senses.PreferredTarget: mind-only three realms and consciousness-only myriad things
AlternateTargets: three realms are mind alone and all things are consciousness alone
Senses.Note: The entry reports how the paired wording is tested in these records; it does not import a general consciousness system as the definition of Zen.

Senses.Explanation: The paired assertion places the three realms under mind and the myriad things under consciousness; Chan records characteristically quote it in order to question, test, qualify, or reverse a lecturer’s ready explanation. Dizang Guichen points to a courtyard stone and asks whether it is inside or outside mind. Huangbo Xiyun says the pair is still language addressed to an opposing view, while Huqiu Shaolong places it in a five-house exchange. Linji Yixuan recites it within a longer address; Yunmen Wenyan refuses the question framed by it, and Chaozong Tongren turns it into a case verse.
